verdict.rationale: Hightouch's core reverse ETL model directly matches this story: models are defined via SQL/dbt/BI queries on existing warehouse tables (docs-2, docs-23), audiences/segments are built on warehouse data without copying it elsewhere (docs-44, docs-19, docs-47), and syncs activate that data to destinations using CDC so only warehouse changes are pushed (docs-25, docs-58). Community corroboration confirms the declarative SQL-model-to-destination mapping and warehouse/S3-only storage architecture (hightouch-comm-2, hightouch-comm-3). missing for 10: independent hands-on benchmarking of warehouse-native performance at scale, and clearer evidence that audience/segment building itself (vs. syncing) never requires data egress before activation.
